items.title: The three shared quantities XRP-101 did not compare
items.hypothesis: immunity_applicable, the T5 floor, and unbound_root_weight are each implemented in more than one of {research aggregator, knowledge-ledger evaluator, Gate} and their agreement has never been measured. XRP-101 found one of three compared quantities diverging (conversions_to_reverse absent from Gate, pricing the central threat at ~2x); the base rate for the unmeasured three is not obviously better.
items.discriminatingTest: Same method as XRP-101: enumerate configurations, evaluate each quantity in every repository that implements it on identical inputs, and require exact agreement -- or a recorded, reasoned divergence. immunity_applicable is the sharpest of the three because T1's precondition depends on it, so a disagreement there is a disagreement about when the immunity theorem applies at all.
items.whyItMatters: XRP-101 established that a quantity named by the paper and implemented in several repositories is verified by no single repository's suite. That rule is general; the audit that produced it was not. Three quantities remain in exactly the state Gate's conversions_to_reverse was in the day before it was checked.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether the products' published safety claims are sound, and whether cross-repository agreement needs enforcing in CI rather than by periodic audit.
items.cost: small -- one focused run; the XRP-101 harness generalises
items.safety: none engaged; findings may require public corrections in Gate/Border as XRP-101 did, which is owner-gated

items.title: Cross-implementation reproduction of LIN-000
items.hypothesis: The independent implementer (or a fourth implementation) reproduces LIN-000's counts from REGISTRATION.md alone -- the draw schedule is registered in prose this time, so unlike KL-000's randomized phase (F11), the randomized counts SHOULD be reproducible cross-implementation, which would be the program's first cross-implementation randomized reproduction.
items.discriminatingTest: Identical exhaustive counters (50,362-world partition) and identical randomized counters from seed 20260808 under the registered schedule.
items.whyItMatters: Tests whether registering a draw schedule actually buys cross-implementation randomized reproducibility (the F11 repair hypothesis) on a small, fresh experiment before committing KL-000 to it.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether BL-016/F11's repair direction (register schedules) is adopted program-wide.
items.cost: one commission under LEAK-101/LEAK-102 packaging rules
